content:
Yesterday, Apple announced a price increase for Apple Music and two Apple One bundle plans.

Apple currently offers a wide range of services, from Apple TV to Apple Music, Apple Fitness+, and more. Apple One bundles these services together so you can enjoy them at a lower price.

Is Apple One worth buying? Here's what you need to know.

Apple's services

As a quick recap, the services Apple currently offers include:

  • Apple Music: Apple's music streaming service with access to over 100 million songs. $11.99 per month
  • Apple TV: Watch popular shows and movies like Ted Lasso, Severance, and more. $12.99 per month
  • Apple Fitness+: Apple's digital fitness platform offering video workouts across 12 different training types. $9.99 per month
  • Apple Arcade: A gaming subscription service with over 200 games, all free of in-app purchases and ads. $6.99 per month
  • Apple News+: Get top headlines from leading newspapers and magazines, daily puzzles, curated recipes, and more. $12.99 per month
  • iCloud+: iCloud storage, Apple Invitations, iCloud Private Relay, Hide My Email, custom email domains, and HomeKit Secure Video. $0.99/month (50GB), $2.99/month (200GB), $9.99/month (2TB)

Apple One bundles

Apple offers three tiers of Apple One: Individual, Family, and Premier, bundling up to six Apple subscription services into one price.

Apple One Individual (save $13/month)

  • Apple TV
  • Apple Music
  • Apple Arcade
  • iCloud+ 50GB storage

Total if purchased separately: $32.96

Apple One Individual price: $19.95

Apple One Family (save $15/month)

Share the following services with up to five people:

  • Apple TV
  • Apple Music
  • Apple Arcade
  • iCloud+ 200GB storage

Total if purchased separately: $42.96

Apple One Family price: $27.95

Apple One Premier (save $33/month)

  • Apple TV
  • Apple Music
  • Apple Arcade
  • Apple Fitness+
  • Apple News+
  • iCloud+ 2TB storage

Total if purchased separately: $72.94

Apple One Premier price: $39.95

Is Apple One right for you?

This question mainly depends on which Apple services you find useful, but you should also consider the math.

For example, if you already subscribe to Apple TV and Apple Music, you should definitely switch to Apple One Individual. Besides saving on your Apple Music and Apple TV subscriptions, you'll also unlock more iCloud storage and features, plus Apple Arcade.

Furthermore, Apple recently raised the price of Apple Music. Interestingly, although the top two Apple One plans have become more expensive due to this price hike, the price of Apple One Individual has remained unchanged. So its value is even better than before.

I encourage everyone to look at the bundle plans and individual service prices above, and do the math for yourself and your family. I'm confident that many of you reading this will save money by switching to one of the Apple One plans. Alternatively, if you've been considering subscribing to a new service, the Apple One discount might make that decision easier.

In particular, Apple TV has been offering increasingly better value. This year, the service added live F1 and MLS broadcasts without raising prices. If you've been on the fence about subscribing to Apple TV, Apple One might make it easier to accept the additional subscription cost.

Are you an Apple One subscriber? If so, which services do you mainly use? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
